verdict: STERIS grew revenue 9% to $1.6B as Life Sciences jumped 18% on strong equipment orders, and management raised its full-year outlook — with a new restructuring plan adding about $25M of charges in the quarter.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; constant-currency organic growth was 8%

kpis.label: Life Sciences revenue
kpis.note: +18% YoY, with capital equipment revenue up 53%

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: for the first half of fiscal 2027, after capital spending

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.note: Sterilizers, surgical products and services for hospitals — service revenue and consumables each grew 10%, capital equipment 4%.

segments.name: Applied Sterilization Technologies
segments.note: Contract sterilization services for medical-device and pharmaceutical makers, sold under the AST name.

segments.name: Life Sciences
segments.note: Equipment and consumables for drug and laboratory production — capital equipment revenue jumped 53%, the standout of the quarter.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs — running sales, service and head-office functions.

opex.name: R&D
opex.note: Research and development of new sterilization and infection-prevention products.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Restructuring expenses recorded in the quarter as STERIS realigns facilities and its product range.

footerNote: STERIS reports in tenths of a million dollars; figures here are rounded to the nearest $1M. Net income of $214M is after $0.4M attributable to noncontrolling interests, which rounds to zero at this scale.

takeaways.title: Life Sciences leads the quarter
takeaways.text: Life Sciences revenue rose 18% to $171M as capital equipment sales jumped 53%, and its operating income climbed to $76M — strong enough for STERIS to raise the segment's full-year expectations.

takeaways.title: Healthcare stays the core
takeaways.text: Healthcare, about 71% of revenue, grew 9% to $1,122M on 10% growth in both services and consumables, with operating income of $269M.

takeaways.title: A new restructuring plan starts
takeaways.text: STERIS approved another targeted restructuring — facility realignment and product rationalization, mainly in Healthcare — booking about $25M of charges in the quarter toward an expected $45M total, for about $9M of annual savings.

oneTimers: About $25M of restructuring charges in the quarter, including a new targeted plan (facility realignment, product rationalization and organizational changes, mainly in Healthcare) expected to cost about $45M in total, of which about $10M is cash.
Amortization of acquired intangible assets was $65M in the quarter — a non-cash cost of past acquisitions that STERIS excludes from its adjusted results.
